81322.subject: Urgent Railway security update: Your workspace may be at risk
81322.body:
Railway Logo

We’re following up on Railway’s October 21st security disclosure ( https://blog.railway.com/p/security-disclosure-wednesday-october-21st?utm_campaign=AI+%26+Cloud+Key+Pattern+%E2%80%94+Security+Follow-up+%E2%80%94+2026-10-23&utm_content=AI+%26+Cloud+Key+Pattern+%E2%80%94+Security+Follow-up+%E2%80%94+2026-10-23&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ) because you are an administrator of the Railway workspace novosadovo's Projects, which we believe to be of interest to the threat actor.

We cannot confirm whether credentials in your workspace were accessed, but we’re notifying you because your environment variables match a pattern the attacker used to search for AI and cloud provider API keys.

We believe this to be the case because your workspace contains variables matching a pattern the attacker used to target customers.

This is not a new incident; this is an update related to the existing disclosure we published on October 21st. If you already taken steps to protect yourself, no further action is required. You can read the preliminary report here ( https://blog.railway.com/p/preliminary-report-october-security-incident?utm_campaign=AI+%26+Cloud+Key+Pattern+%E2%80%94+Security+Follow-up+%E2%80%94+2026-10-23&utm_content=AI+%26+Cloud+Key+Pattern+%E2%80%94+Security+Follow-up+%E2%80%94+2026-10-23&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ).

To recap, what we definitively know so far:

* Threat intelligence suggests the actor was specifically targeting environments with AI API keys or cloud provider API keys.
* Your workspace contains environment variables matching that search pattern.
* We cannot confirm whether or not your secret environment variables were decrypted.

As such, it would be prudent for you to take the following actions as soon as possible:

* Rotate sensitive credentials — such as API keys, database passwords, and access tokens stored in Railway environment variables.
* Update your Railway variables and redeploy dependent services — You should coordinate database credential changes with the applications that use them.
* Review provider activity and audit logs; especially AI keys — Check GitHub ( https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/reviewing-your-security-log?utm_campaign=AI+%26+Cloud+Key+Pattern+%E2%80%94+Security+Follow-up+%E2%80%94+2026-10-23&utm_content=AI+%26+Cloud+Key+Pattern+%E2%80%94+Security+Follow-up+%E2%80%94+2026-10-23&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ) and registries such as Docker Hub for unfamiliar access, unexpected usage, or unauthorized changes.

As of October 22 at 03:32 UTC, we are no longer under direct attack and have strengthened protections around the affected systems. We will additionally contact you directly if we establish specific impact to your workspace.

We’re sorry about the incident and the burden it created for you and your organization. For help with rotation, or to report suspicious activity,

81070.subject: 💰 The Funding: What happens if MSCI drops crypto treasuries like Strategy?
81070.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c1c9af72-58d8-47c5-88eb-8e5007f7e3dc/unnamed__17_.png?t=1789144554)
Caption: 

Written by Yogita Khatri  | Edited by Zack Abrams

———————————————————————————

Presented By:

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0f002faa-88b1-4362-8467-fbc25a6c61ee/Screenshot_2026-10-16_at_4.02.56_PM__3___1___1___1_.png?t=1792184177)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

----------
Happy Sunday, and welcome to the 62nd edition of [The Funding](https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/the-funding)!

MSCI [finalized rules](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-10-15-msci-rules-could-exclude-strategy-mstr-from-indexes-418729) on Oct. 15 that could push Strategy and other crypto treasury companies out of its main global indexes as soon as Nov. 30. What would that mean for how these companies raise money, and is anyone still willing to fund them? I caught up with investors and analysts to find out.

Let's get into it.


----------———————————————————————————

----------
# THE INSIDE VIEW

## What if MSCI drops crypto treasuries?


----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2012e140-bc90-4ae9-b029-9f403353161b/Dat-Image-1200x675.jpg?t=1792371900)
Caption: 

----------
Index provider MSCI recently [approved new rules](https://app2.msci.com/webapp/index_ann/DocGet?pub_key=aq0wbkjxPgo%3D&lang=en&format=html) that target "non-operating" companies, which mainly hold assets instead of running a business, such as digital asset treasury firms, or DATs.

Under the new rules, MSCI will first check whether a company has substantial operating assets, such as equipment or inventory. In the [proposal MSCI published in August](https://www.msci.com/downloads/documents/indexes/consultations/equity/Consultation%20on%20Eligibility%20of%20Non-Operating%20Companies%20for%20the%20%20MSCI%20Global%20Investable%20Market%20Indexes.pdf), that meant operating assets making up more than half of total assets. Companies that fail this check face five financial tests, which in the proposal included whether a company generates operating cash flow and how much it relies on raising capital to buy assets. Those flagged on four or more will be excluded.

Current index members get some leeway: they will be removed only if they fail in both of their two most recent annual filing periods. If they fail in only one, they stay in the index unless they fail the following year. Companies not yet in the index are blocked if they fail in either of the last two years.

In a simulation published in August using May data, MSCI flagged two bitcoin treasury companies, Michael Saylor's Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet, for potential exclusion. Ethereum treasury firm SharpLink
